savings.reason: Section 1 preserves pending and prior-act proceedings, matured rights and duties and incurred penalties; it also continues restrictions on property still blocked. These are material residuals, not an unqualified disappearance of every sanction.

research_rationale: The full original declares an emergency as well as blocking property and prescribing sanctions. EO:12724 section 6 revokes only inconsistent portions, effective immediately on August 9, 1990; it carries administrative actions forward and saves violations. It is not a whole-order end. EO:12771 expressly preserves the Iraqi emergency while revoking the Kuwaiti orders. EO:12817 adds asset-transfer machinery; it is not a global termination of EO:12722. EO:13303 section 2(a) removes the section 1 described property from application of EO:12722 as of its effective date while section 2(b) preserves other administrative actions. EO:13350 ends the emergency and revokes the order at 12:01 a.m. EDT July 30, 2004, not its July 29 signing date, but continues certain blocked-property restrictions and saves accrued actions and liabilities. Neither that later outside bound nor incomplete current-law pointers establishes all earliest clause ends in the presence of the specifically unheld EO:12743.
